meetings.headline: Town meeting rejected a $986,000 ARPA-vs-stabilization-fund transfer for a new ambulance and dump trucks.
meetings.summary: This special town meeting acted on sixteen warrant articles: it approved FY24 budget adjustments including a town-clerk raise (despite objections over an executive-session vote), funded a clerical union contract and a police opioid co-response program, funded primary-school air conditioning after rejecting amendments tying it to a grant, and passed a roof repair, a Marshall Park grant-qualifying article, and several zoning bylaw changes (water supply protection map rewrite passed over, farm definition, common driveways, solar parking canopies). The one clear rejection was Article 4, a $986,000 transfer from the special purpose stabilization fund to reimburse ARPA-funded ambulance and dump truck purchases, which failed after debate over control of ARPA spending by the select board versus town meeting.

what_happened.line: Town meeting voted down a transfer from the special purpose stabilization fund meant to reimburse ARPA-funded purchases of an ambulance and two dump trucks, 29-92.
Town meeting approved FY24 budget adjustments, including a town clerk salary increase, 126-13, after residents objected that the raise had been discussed in executive session.
Town meeting funded the first year of the clerical union contract, 132-11, after public comment that clerical wages lag comparable towns.
Town meeting approved a transfer for ductless mini-split air conditioning at the primary school after voting down two amendments that would have tied the funding to a Green Communities grant.
Several zoning bylaw changes passed by the required two-thirds margin, including a farm-definition update, common-driveway provisions, and solar parking canopy rules.

why_it_matters: The rejected transfer leaves the ambulance and dump-truck purchases without an approved funding source and keeps the special purpose stabilization fund at its current balance rather than drawing it down.
The town clerk raise and the clerical union contract affect town payroll costs and, indirectly, what the town needs to raise going forward.
The air-conditioning vote and the failed grant-first amendments determine whether primary-school cooling work proceeds now or waits on a separate grant application.

meetings.headline: Town Meeting passed the FY24 town and school budget and created a new senior property tax exemption program
meetings.summary: Lunenburg's Annual Town Meeting worked through 22 warrant articles: a consent calendar of routine transfers, the FY24 town and school operating budget, a large transfer to the overlay account to cover FY23 tax abatements, the FY24 capital plan, union and salary-plan wage increases, new special-purpose, OPEB and opioid-settlement stabilization funds, the sewer enterprise budget, a new means-tested senior property tax exemption requiring state special legislation, and a zoning bylaw change to allow self-storage by special permit. Finance Director Karen Brochu was honored on her last town meeting before retiring after 38 years.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting approved the FY24 town and school operating budget, 98-8, meeting the two-thirds threshold required.
Voters approved a transfer from free cash into the overlay account to cover FY23 tax abatements, 98-12.

Town Meeting voted to petition the state for a means-tested senior property tax exemption, amended so its cost is shared by all property classes rather than residential alone; the outcome was not clearly stated on the recording.
The FY24 capital plan, fire union and salary-plan wage increases, and new OPEB and opioid-settlement stabilization funds all passed.
A zoning bylaw change allowing self-storage by special permit passed 66-8.

why_it_matters: The approved FY24 budget sets town and school spending for the year, the appropriation behind residents' tax bills.
The senior tax exemption, if the state grants the requested legislation, would shift some property tax burden onto other households -- a tradeoff several residents debated on the floor.
The overlay transfer and capital plan commit a large share of free cash up front, which a resident argued leaves other needs, including deteriorating capital projects, underfunded.
